data: Which sampling strategy has the highest F1-score after 8 iterations without bigram features?

The question asks for the sampling strategy with the highest F1-score after 8 iterations without bigram features. From the caption, we know that the comparison is made when the ratio of initial labeled set and unlabeled set is 3:7. The figure shows two graphs: one for "Without Bigram Features" and another for "With Bigram Features". We need to focus on the left graph since the question specifies "without bigram features".

Looking at the left graph, the lines represent different sampling strategies: LC (red), RAND (orange), MTE (blue), MTM (green), and NE-LP (purple). The y-axis represents the F1-score in percentage, and the x-axis represents the number of iterations. After 8 iterations, the line representing NE-LP (purple) appears to be the highest among all the lines. Therefore, the NE-LP strategy has the highest F1-score after 8 iterations without bigram features.
